cohort: Second-born, term, singleton offspring delivered between January 1, 1993 and December 31, 2007 in Scotland, UK, to women with a history of CS
finding: Compared to VBAC, both planned and unscheduled repeat CS were associated with an increased risk of hospitalization with asthma, while unscheduled repeat CS was also associated with increased risk of learning disability and death.
mod_finding: Children born by repeat cesarean section, whether planned or unscheduled, had an increased risk of hospitalization with asthma compared to children born vaginally after a previous cesarean section.
